measurements.question: What value lands on the last bar for request.security(sym, "D", close) on an intraday chart and request.security(sym, "30", close) on a daily chart, historical versus realtime; what the default lookahead and gaps arguments do; and what comes back before the requested series has its first bar.

allowed: the LAST 30-minute bar of that day
the FIRST 30-minute bar of that day

measurements.notes: PARTIAL — the HISTORICAL half is measured, the realtime half is not (market closed, 2026-09-19 evening). Measured on a 5m NASDAQ:NVDA chart, last bar 09-18 15:55 ET. LAST BAR: a "D" request returns the SAME day's daily bar (time 09-18 09:30 ET) with close 222.27, and lookahead_on and gaps_on give the same value there. MID-SESSION (bar 09-18 12:35 ET, 40 bars back): the default returns the PREVIOUS day's daily bar (09-17 09:30 ET, close 219.34) while lookahead_on returns TODAY's (222.27). So on a historical intraday bar the default hands you the previous COMPLETED daily bar; only the live bar sees the forming one. ALSO: the last 5m bar's close (222.08) is NOT the daily close (222.27) — the daily carries the 16:00 print, so daily values must come from the daily series, never from the last intraday bar. STILL OWED: the realtime last-bar behaviour during an open session, the "30"-from-daily direction, and the value before a requested series' first bar. Rig: NASDAQ:NVDA on the UCT CAPTURE RIG layout (01f1AcIj), TV Premium, user TSDR_TRADING

measurements.question: Is a wrong-exchange spelling invalid -- NASDAQ:JPM, where JPM is NYSE-listed -- and what does ignore_invalid_symbol = true then yield?
measurements.notes: PARTIAL - the ignore_invalid_symbol half is measured, part A is not. On a 5m NVDA chart: request.security("NASDAQ:JPM", "D", close, ignore_invalid_symbol = true) returned na, while the control request.security("NYSE:JPM", ...) returned 349.67 on the same bar, and a deliberately impossible NASDAQ:ZZZZZZ also returned na. So a wrong-exchange spelling IS an invalid symbol, and with ignore_invalid_symbol it yields na rather than erroring. The control is what makes this an EXCHANGE fact rather than a broken request. Consequence: the RVOL dashboard prefixes bare tickers with NASDAQ:, so every NYSE-listed name in a pasted watchlist yields na and is dropped by the script own na filter. STILL OWED: part A — the same request WITHOUT ignore_invalid_symbol, and its verbatim error text. Rig: NASDAQ:NVDA on the UCT CAPTURE RIG layout (01f1AcIj), TV Premium, user TSDR_TRADING

measurements.question: When array.sort_indices meets equal keys, in what order do their original indices come out?
measurements.notes: PARTIAL — measured with array.from(3.0, 1.0, 1.0, 2.0), ties planted at indices 1 and 2: ascending returned 1,2,3,0 and descending returned 0,3,2,1. So ties keep their ORIGINAL order when ascending and appear REVERSED when descending — descending behaves as the reverse of the ascending order, not as a stable sort. STILL OWED: the all-equal array case and the already-descending control. Rig: NASDAQ:NVDA on the UCT CAPTURE RIG layout (01f1AcIj), TV Premium, user TSDR_TRADING

measurements.question: Inside a requested context, does timeframe.period report the requested timeframe or the chart's?
measurements.notes: PART A MEASURED, part B not. On a 5-MINUTE chart (chart timeframe.period = 5), inside a request.security(syminfo.tickerid, "D", ...): timeframe.multiplier = 1, timeframe.isdaily = 1, timeframe.isintraday = 0. So timeframe.* reflects the REQUESTED context, not the chart's. The 5m chart is what makes this distinguishable — on a daily chart both readings agree and the test proves nothing. STILL OWED: part B, whether a string-returning request of timeframe.period compiles. Rig: NASDAQ:NVDA on the UCT CAPTURE RIG layout (01f1AcIj), TV Premium, user TSDR_TRADING

measurements.question: What does hour(time, "America/New_York") do across a US daylight-saving boundary, including the repeated autumn hour?

live_bar_hour_default_tz.value: 15:55 — identical to NY, so the default timezone is the exchange timezone

allowed: yes - the same UTC instant maps to a different NY hour across the boundary
dst_is_respected.value: yes - the same UTC instant maps to a different NY hour across the boundary

repeated_hour_behaviour.value: the 02:00 hour does not exist in spring (06:00Z->1:00, 07:00Z->3:00) and 1:00 occurs twice in autumn (both 05:00Z and 06:00Z report 1:0); hour() reports local wall-clock time and does not disambiguate the repeat

measurements.notes: Built on timestamp() with fixed UTC instants, so the answer does not depend on loaded history. syminfo.timezone read as America/New_York on the same table. Rig: NASDAQ:NVDA on the UCT CAPTURE RIG layout (01f1AcIj), TV Premium, user TSDR_TRADING
